text:
Dear Mr Zimmermann,

Nothing was forced. I want to say that first, because I know it matters. It was a very hot night, 18 to 19 August 2026, and I'd left the terrace door of my ground-floor flat wide open to get some air while I slept. Someone simply walked in from the garden through the open door. I didn't hear a thing.

My handbag was on the chair by the terrace door, and my keys were in it: flat door, front door of the building and letterbox. Rosenau Cooperative, who own the building, had the cylinders of my flat door and the front door changed the next day and charged me CHF 525. I'd like that included in my claim.

I'm enclosing a list of the stolen things with their values, CHF 4,750 altogether, and the purchase receipts for the handbag, the phone and the laptop.

This all happened at home, in my flat at Sonnenweg 77 in Kreuzlingen.

I should also tell you that I cleaned up the next morning before I'd thought it through. The things the thief didn't want, my diary, make-up and some papers from the handbag, were scattered across the terrace and there were muddy footprints on the floor by the door. I picked everything up and mopped the floor, so none of that can be seen any more. I'm sorry, I just couldn't bear looking at it.

Kind regards,
Eva Ellis
